text:
Alex: quick q — when the console shows an SLO alert preview, who actually 'gets' the notification by default? tenant owner only, or the full route/escalation matrix? we need a clear default for previews + rollouts.
Maria: we currently show a 'notify' preview badge but it never calls the notify service. it's purely a UI hint. customers read it as 'this will page people' which has caused confusion.
Ken: +1. that mismatch bit us during the last canary — folks thought they'd be paged. options: 1) make preview actionable (call notify API) or 2) change language and surface computed recipients only. i prefer 2.
Rachel: proposal: keep previews non-actionable, but surface "effective recipients" computed by the routing service. show reasons (owner, escalation, fallback) and any quiet-window suppression. tooltip: "this is who would be notified if this alert fired right now."
Alex: who owns the computation though? routing-service has final logic (weights, quiet windows, per-tenant overrides). console could duplicate logic but that's a maintenance footgun.
Maria: agree. prefer console call into routing-service for a read-only preview endpoint. avoids duplication but we must be careful about latency and auth.
Ken: API proposal: lightweight `GET /v1/notify/preview?rule_id=...&at=...` returning recipients + explanation list. keep it read-only, cacheable, tenant-scoped. routing-service retains decision logic.
Rachel: UI needs: small sample of channels (e.g., PagerDuty, Slack, email), the escalation step, and any suppression reason like `quiet_window` or `snoozed`. also add telemetry fields so we can audit why someone would/ wouldn't receive a page.
Alex: example response we want (conceptual): `recipients: [{name: "oncall-team", channel: "pagerduty", reason: "escalation-step-1"}, {name: "tenant-owner", channel: "email", reason: "owner-rule"}]`, plus `suppressed: [{who: "infra-oncall", reason: "quiet_window"}]`.
Maria: also think about canary rollouts: if rule is in a canary with 10% sampling, preview should reflect deterministic sampling (so same subset shows up each preview for a given seed). routing-service must support deterministic sampling param for preview.
Ken: ACLs — only tenant admins or members with policy X can call preview. and add `preview=true` tag to telemetry so these calls don't count as real alerts/incidents.
Rachel: UI note: show a small badge if preview used deterministic sampling vs full fanout. helps set expectations during rollouts.
Alex: agree. ops asks: make sure preview calls are cheap and cached for ~30s to avoid thundering. can we reuse existing routing caches?
Maria: yes, but we should add a short TTL and include `preview` in cache key. also record a lightweight audit log entry for each preview call.
Ken: i'll draft the API RFC with ACLs + sampling + caching notes. Maria/Rachel can append UI and telemetry parts.
Alex: thanks — quick follow-up: can someone create the issue?
deploy-bot: created issue PLAT-4823: add `notify/preview` read-only API for console previews — https://issues/redwood/PLAT-4823
Ken: :thumbsup:
Rachel: added a comment on PLAT-4823 with UI mockups and tooltip copy.
Maria: i'll add telemetry fields and audit entry shape to the RFC.
Alex: perfect. let's sync in the RFC PR tomorrow and try to land basics before the next canary.
